label: AFFECTION

cover.headline: 5 thank-yous that mean more than *“thanks”*
cover.sub: Appreciation works best when it’s specific.

points.heading: For the invisible work
points.body: The things that only get noticed when they don’t happen. Notice one out loud.
points.panel: “Thanks for always making sure the car has gas.”

points.heading: For who he is
points.body: Not only what he does. Name a quality you’d miss.
points.panel: “I love how patient you are with my mom.”

points.heading: In front of others
points.body: A kind word in front of the kids or friends means a little more.
points.panel: “Dad fixed that for us. Wasn’t that nice of him?”

points.heading: For the effort
points.body: Even when it didn’t quite work out. Trying deserves to be seen.
points.panel: “I saw how hard you tried to make tonight nice.”

points.heading: For something from long ago
points.body: Something from years back that you still carry. He may not know it stuck.
points.panel: “I still think about how you showed up when my dad was sick.”

close.save: Save this for a day he needs to hear it.

caption:
“Thanks” is polite. A specific thank-you is something else. It tells him you noticed, and being noticed is a quiet kind of closeness.

You don’t need all five. Pick the one that’s true today and say it out loud.

Save this for later, and follow @spotseason for more small steps.
